description: No candidate has a numeric attendance estimate. The Sweida reports range from “limited”/“several” to “large crowds,” and the northeast reports give no numbers. None establishes 50 attendees at a site.
required_followup: Seek additional contemporary local reporting or visual records with a defensible count; do not convert qualitative crowd words into numbers.

description: E001 is a solidarity reception at a private home, leaving public-forum status and the exact demand at that occurrence uncertain.
required_followup: Confirm whether the Jan 26 reception was open/public and whether its attendees directly made the apology demand.

description: The Jan 26 Qanawat reception and Jan 27 Suwayda city/roundabout gatherings concern the same insult but have distinct reported dates and locations; coordination, overlap, and episode separation are not fully resolved.
required_followup: Compare additional dated reports and the unavailable supplementary Coding Procedure; retain the candidates separately pending review.

description: No candidate has a supported physical end date. Feb 2 calls to calm and reports of normal life or a lifted siege are not proof that a particular gathering ended then.
required_followup: Find explicit reporting that attendees departed, dispersed, or ended the gathering; do not infer a month-end or use a later official announcement as endpoint.

description: Al-Araby attributes the Jan 26 Qanawat arrivals, Damascus intervention, release of a previously detained man, and Luay al-Ali’s apology to local sources. The Jan 27 official delegation visit is separately reported as a de-escalation attempt; 7al says it produced no result, but whether officials actually met protest representatives is unclear. Other response dimensions remain unreported.
required_followup: Verify whether the local-source account can be independently tied to Jan 26 and whether Jan 27 officials actually met protest representatives; never code the prior Homs detention as event arrests.

description: E003 and E004 oppose a siege policy attributed to SDF/AANES/Asayish, de facto authorities in fragmented-control areas. The project has no calibrated rule here for treating that policy as a domestic Syrian-state target.
required_followup: Obtain coordinator review against the project’s domestic-state-target rule; do not treat de facto control alone as sufficient.

description: North Press says Asayish intervention cut short the Jan 27 gatherings; for Jan 31 it reports an armed clash after an attempted march. Whether Asayish activity qualifies as a state response and whether any action directly dispersed marchers are unresolved.
required_followup: Find event-specific detail on what Asayish did to participants and obtain actor calibration before coding a state response.

description: The Jan 31 source reports a death of a regime-affiliated fighter and unspecified injuries in an armed Asayish–National Defense firefight. These are not attributed to protester violence or state action against demonstrators.
required_followup: Keep the firefight excluded as combat unless a source independently documents civilian protest casualties or action directed at demonstrators.

description: The SOHR-hosted Sweida article credits Asharq Al-Awsat; the original Asharq result was not opened. The two North Press teacher reports share one agency, and the Feb 2 siege follow-ups report overlapping official statements.
required_followup: Map bylines, republication, and common statement origins before counting corroboration; do not count same-agency or same-source accounts as independent confirmation.

description: Shafaq, SyriacPress Arabic, and a separate Jan 26 7al item returned web-tool Cache misses when opened; the original Asharq English page was search-only. These are not verified site-level access denials.
required_followup: If those leads remain material, attempt one ordinary request to each exact public URL under the public-source rule; respect any actual denial and do not use a mirror or bypass.

description: Discovery used Arabic and English plus Kurmanji and French queries; source interpretation was not independently reviewed by a fluent human linguist. Coverage in other locally relevant languages is not demonstrated.
required_followup: Have Arabic and Kurmanji evidence checked by a qualified reviewer and extend local-language discovery if resources allow.

description: Open-web searches surfaced Suwayda, Hasakah/Qamishli, and a February Idlib lead; other governorates and control zones were searched unevenly. No relevant Jan event being found in a region is not evidence that none occurred there.
required_followup: Continue province-by-province and control-zone searches, especially for local outlet and sector-specific reports, without treating a fixed query count as coverage.

description: The 26 queries used open-web search; the protocol’s LexisNexis universe is unavailable. Search result total counts were not exposed, and some queries may omit or misdate relevant material.
required_followup: Retain query logs and obtain the original archival method only if authorized access becomes available; do not claim exhaustive coverage.

description: Official latest Dataverse event bytes, current universe/schema, reuse terms, and the standalone supplementary Coding Procedure remain unresolved under the unit’s pending official-baseline gate.
required_followup: Coordinator must verify the authoritative current files/universe, reuse terms, and supplementary procedure before any integration; this worker did not repeat denied official-data retrievals.
